reviews.review:
Not to just go into all the positives, I thought I should address many of the things that are (and mostly perceived as) negatives as an objective look so you can form your own ideas.

Grinding: 

While it IS true that there is a lot of mission running and material collecting to do in order to get weapons, gear and  frames, you should never feel like you HAVE to get things beyond your level bracket. There are various affordable in game credit weapons and cheap blueprints for early strong loadouts. You can craft Extractor Drones that will mine a system for resourecs once you complete said system and have it greatly aid in crafting what you need.

The major negative in all of this is there is not a lot of consistency on what exactly will drop because of two factors:

1. There is no guarantee that the enemy that carries the mod/component you are looking for will appear in a given map, even if the map belongs to the faction said enemy is a part of.

2. If the enemy does show up, there is no guarantee that the drops will have the items you need and may have to run missions multiple times if you are looking for something very specific.

(This has been recently alleviated with the new void relic system, which allows you to tailor the drop percentage of specific items in the Void by contributing various relics.)

F2P or P2Win?:

I have seen this time and time again, any form of shop that sells any currency or booster or weapon is seen as a P2W "scheme". In reality it is basically down to time spent=free items, money spent=more free time. There is NOTHING in the game that is relevant to advancement and gameplay that you cannot get through playing the game itself. 

Exceptions to this are special event only weapons/mods/Blueprints, Store credit and XP boosters ( just increases the rate at which you gain XP or credits but you still have to PLAY for them to work), slots for weapon/warframe/sentinel storage (relevant to gameplay because you limit your versatility if you cannot have a variety of available options at hand.)

To address These concerns however, the trading system was put into place to alleviate some of the grindy randomness of certain mods or parts. This is sometimes seen as another game breaking drawback, but if you realize that it alleviates the most glaring one then you would be hard pressed to deny its usefulness. 

You can trade any unwanted mods, keys, Prime Blueprints/parts/whole weapons or warframes for credits, other similar items you do not have and Platinum, the store currency. This means you do not have to EVER spend any money on the game if you are savvy with trading and accumulate enough items to sell/trade, thus making the drop rates work for you. You can use this platinum to purchase slots for your loadouts, cosmetic items or whatever your heart desires from the store.

"Bad" Community:

This should not even be a true drawback of the game because I see it as unfair to blame the developers for something that is within our responsibilities as gamers. The devs should allow every possibility of fair play and teamwork but as the saying goes "You can lead a horse to water, but you can't make them drink it", so goes that "You can lead a gamer to a working group, but you can't make them participate". 

A lot of the content is much better with a group and yields better drops and more XP, and some you NEED a group for, like certain defense missions or the carrying of 4 different dragon keys to open up the vault in a Void mission. What we need to do is make sure we have high standards for BEHAVIOUR of the people we play with rather than the gear or "skillz". Equipment and skill can be learned, personality cannot be unlearned in most cases. 

Use the ignore feature if someone behaves or doesn't play to your liking, you don't hinder their gameplay by reporting them but they don't hinder yours by not showing up in any games you queue up in. A vote kick feature could be useful in situations where a player is extremely toxic but these systems tend to get abused and serve to punish the victims more often than not.

Boring Levels:

I admit, early in the game's development I thought the tilesets were just bland endless halls and for the most part, they indeed were! But at this stage the art team has increased the variety and unique look of each system you go to so as to have a lot of open and large areas and not so repetitive layouts ( except when the layout is paramount to the mission itself). Remember, this is a game with randomly generated maps in the style of Diablo/Torchlight so it DOES have set structures of rooms that interconnect to create levels. 

Levels themselves suffer from a twofold problem most of the time, which is people rush through them and do not let new players familiarize themselves with each room and that a lot of secret reas and loot are avoided by this constant hurry and the lack of drive to explore. We have ourselves as well as the devs to blame in certain amounts. The in centive to explore is definitely there for the completionist at heart, you can go around scanning everything with your codex scanner and fill your index with lots of nice info but, people rarely stop for these players long enough for them to find any secret or scan anything. 
This goes hand in hand with the previous statement about grouping, Make sure you are with likeminded gamers and make a few friends or bring some into the game so you all have a nice tight group. You can all explore and reap every nook and cranny of a level. It may take more time, but time spent with friends in a game you like playing is never a waste, and you will see that all the extra materials and credits add up so you can upgrade even faster.

What Lore?:

This is also a prevalent issue against the game, "nonexistent" lore or a paper-thin plot. Early in the game's development the story itself was very basic and vague, partially because of it being early and partially on purpose to preserve an air of mystery.

The story vaguely conected to the previous Digital Extremes game Dark Sector (Hence the Tenno being named after Dark Sector's main protagonist) with recent hints at a true confirmation on how the games have a linked story. On it's own though, tha game has  a fair amount of lore if you care to look for it. Codex scans done on prime warframes, boss dialogue, special missions, even the level designs themselves tell parts of a bigger story that is much more well thought out that it would seem, or that a game so action oriented would normally have. 

Though it may seem a bit less scathing than most pro/con reviews, I think this game deserves more than a cursory glance and an offhand dismissal based on it's faults. It is enjoyable, fun (especially with friends), and one of the more unique and high quality F2P games out there, with a very involved and very passionate team behind it.

Hope this review helped and hope to see you in-game, 

Cheers!
